title: Revolutionary Girl Utena
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Orphaned as a child and rescued by a mysterious prince, Utena Tenjou resolves to become a prince herself rather than a princess. At Ohtori Academy she is drawn into sword duels for the 'Rose Bride', Anthy Himemiya, and into the schemes of Anthy's brother Akio (AniList; Viz blurb via MU; ANN review of the five-volume manga).
life_message: A girl can claim courage, agency and loyalty for herself instead of accepting the passive role others assign her.

content.note: Ritual fencing duels (MU Duels, Sword/s; ANN). Gore not reported.
Surreal, manipulative atmosphere; Utena nearly drowned as a child (AniList; MU).

Implied brother-sister incest between Anthy and Akio, and 14-year-old Utena pursued by a high-school senior and a college student (ANN; AniList Incest and Age Gap tags; MU). Some girl/girl kissing (ANN). Explicitness not reported.
Grief and a near-drowning after her parents' deaths (MU blurb says she was about to drown herself); manipulation and abusive sibling (MU).
Manipulative older characters framed as the problem (ANN). A twin-sibling relationship 'played for laughs' (ANN).
Developed alongside the anime by Be-Papas (AniList creators; MU).

dominant: Feminism (gender roles and agency); expressive individualism; critique of the 'bride' ideal

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts settled by sword duels at Ohtori Academy (MU Duels; ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Utena wants 'the masculine privilege of action and agency' (ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Akio-Anthy sibling bond is shown as a trap (ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Student council and duel ranks challenged by Utena (MU Student Council).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Critique of the 'good wife, wise mother' ideal (ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Self-chosen identity as a prince (AniList; MU).

folkways.japan: Plays on the Japanese ryosai kenbo ('good wife, wise mother') ideal and the shoujo 'prince' archetype, described here as context.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls the gender themes 'interesting' and does not call it preachy; says it 'undermines its own message at times.'

personified.ideology: Girls claiming agency instead of a passive role
Enforcing the traditional 'bride' role on women

delivery.note: The gender critique is carried through the duels and Akio's schemes rather than stated in speeches, per the ANN manga review.

winners_losers: Utena's search for agency gets the story's sympathy; Akio's control and the passive-bride ideal are shown as the trap (ANN).
